case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: International Federation of Professional & Technical Engineers, Local 21 v. Superior Court
key_cases.holding: The court held that the names and salaries of individual public employees are subject to disclosure under the California Public Records Act because the public's interest in the information outweighs the employees' privacy interest, and the personnel-file exemption does not shield it.
key_cases.relevance: Is the authority for obtaining the payroll and expenditure records that underlie any independent audit of a county child welfare agency.
key_cases.quote: Balancing these interests, we conclude that disclosure of the salary information at issue in the present case would not constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.

key_cases.case_name: City of San Jose v. Superior Court
key_cases.holding: The court held that writings by public employees concerning the conduct of public business are public records subject to the California Public Records Act even when sent, received or stored on personal accounts or devices.
key_cases.relevance: Extends records access to the internal communications that reveal how audit and financial findings were handled.
key_cases.quote: we hold that a city employee's writings about public business are not excluded from CPRA simply because they have been sent, received, or stored in a personal account.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that states make 'reasonable efforts' to prevent removal and reunify families does not create a right enforceable by beneficiaries under section 1983 or by implied right of action.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms that federal financial oversight is the principal remedy for a state's failure to meet Title IV-E requirements.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.
